title: 3SUM Breaker
one_liner: Watch why shaving an algorithm's exponent from 2.0 to 1.995 saves millions of years of compute at scale.
speaker: Imad Mustak
context: Mustak described an Anthropic model helping mathematicians push the classic 3SUM problem from quadratic (n^2) to subquadratic (n^1.995) time, a result thought impossible for decades.
demo: Visitor drags a slider for input size n and sees two animated bars race: one computing in O(n^2) time, one in O(n^1.995), with a live countdown clock showing operations-per-second on a simulated computer. At large n the 'old' bar visibly stalls out for hypothetical years while the 'new' one finishes in seconds, with a side panel explaining the real 3SUM problem (finding three numbers that sum to zero) in plain language.
data_plan: Simulated data: client-side computation of n^2 vs n^1.995 operation counts converted to estimated wall-clock time at a stated, clearly-labeled hypothetical operations-per-second rate.
risks: Must avoid implying the visualization is literally how the new algorithm works internally — it's a scale demonstration of exponent differences, not a reproduction of the proof.

episode.title: Why Altman Says "Accept Some Bad Things Happening" and What It Means for AI Safety | MOONSHOTS #301
